notes: Small closed vocabularies for training views. Every field allows 'unknown'. Rich open-ended combat descriptions stay in the existing claim records; these labels do not replace them.

clip_context.definition: What kind of footage the 20 s interval is, judged from the frames (not the video title).

pair_configuration.definition: Positional relationship of the primary engaged pair of athletes in this frame. 'no_engagement' when fewer than two athletes are interacting. 'unknown' when occluded/ambiguous.

role.definition: Role of the person in this interval, constant for one identity. 'athlete' = actively competing, sparring or drilling on the mat/cage during this interval (the demonstration partner of an instructor is an athlete). 'instructor' = the person teaching or demonstrating. 'referee' = match official. 'coach_or_corner' = coaching from the side. Anyone only watching, waiting, sitting at the edge, filming or passing through is 'spectator_or_crew', even if dressed to train.

posture.definition: Body orientation of this person in this frame, from visible evidence only. Labelled for athletes, referees and instructors; spectators/crew get 'unknown'.

scope.detection: Every visible person whose body is at least partly visible and not purely a crowd texture is a person instance. Persons on printed graphics/posters/screens are excluded. Spectators and crew are labelled persons with role spectator_or_crew so they are never silent background.
scope.segmentation: Visible-region instance mask per person; overlaps resolved so each pixel belongs to at most one person.
